# Pandamonium v1.0.64

This train closes the Wave 4 batch: the session Details panel now steps out of the way while a side-mounted panel is open, and Pandamonium gains a guided in-app bug report workflow that collects privacy-reviewed evidence and submits it through a server-held GitHub App token. It also carries the composer re-measurement fix that returned `main` CI to green after v1.0.63.

## MAD-856 — Feedback: add guided in-app bug reports with redacted evidence

### Problem

Pandamonium had a structured GitHub bug template but no discoverable in-app way to capture a problem while it was happening. Reports arrived through chat or screenshots without a stable environment snapshot, exact reproduction sequence, correlation identifiers, or duplicate guard, which made them hard to reconcile with the backlog.

### Implementation

Adds a persistent **Report a bug** action that opens a compact right-dock workflow on desktop and a full-width surface on mobile. The three-step guided flow captures summary, goal, expected behavior, actual behavior/error, ordered reproduction steps, workaround, and report type; supports paste/drag/select screenshots with step labels, reorder, and removal; builds a bounded, allowlisted diagnostic bundle (version/revision, install method, OS/browser class, route, correlation identifiers, safe error classification, service health timestamps); redacts secrets, cookies, authorization headers, private content, hostnames, URLs, and local paths before review; shows the exact public title/body and every attachment behind one explicit confirmation; diverts security-vulnerability reports to the private advisory path; performs a bounded duplicate search with link/add-evidence or continue-as-new; and preserves a retryable local draft with exact-once submission. Server-side modules: `src/feedback_report.py` (validation, redaction, allowlist, exact title/body builder, image sniffing), `src/feedback_diagnostics.py`, `src/feedback_store.py` (owner-scoped attachments and the submission index), `src/github_issues.py` (RS256 JWT, cached installation token, bounded search/create/comment/create), and `routes/feedback_routes.py`. The browser never receives or forwards a repository credential. Commits `5bcd066e`, `2d7e208d`, `1c90009e`; PR #229; docs in `docs/feedback-bug-reports.md` and `.env.example`.

### Product value and UI visibility

A discoverable bug-report dock survives in-app navigation, captures ordered checkpoints, previews and annotates screenshots, and returns the exact GitHub issue URL plus a copyable redacted report on success. The review screen states the public visibility before submission, and Linear remains a maintainer-triage action rather than an automatic second ticket.

### Verification

Focused suites report 66 passed covering redaction canaries, the diagnostics allowlist, exact-once and retry behavior, security diversion, JWT/token flow, and a static check that no credential can reach frontend code; adjacent suites report 159 and 29 passed; the browser spec reports 8 passed and 30 passed with adjacent composer/modal specs. The full CI browser suite is green after the composer re-measurement fix in this train.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Live GitHub submission requires an operator-provisioned GitHub App (App id, installation id, private key) installed with **Issues: write** only; provisioning steps and the screenshot-URL caveat are documented. An unconfigured install fails closed with honest copy and preserves the draft. No new dependency beyond the existing `cryptography` stack, no second modal framework, and no continuous capture, keylogging, arbitrary log upload, or automatic public security disclosure.

## MAD-932 — UI: auto-hide the session Details panel while a side-mounted panel is open

### Problem

The session Details panel ("Recent session activity", sources, tools, outputs) stayed visible while Settings and other side-mounted panels opened, crowding the workspace instead of yielding to the active panel.

### Implementation

`static/js/modalSnap.js` now exposes `sidePanelDocked()` and a single `watchSidePanelDock(listener)` observer over the canonical `left/right-dock-active` body state that every dock path (Settings, drag-dock, tile manager, tool windows) already maintains. `static/js/conversationContext.js` consumes it: the Details panel auto-hides when a dock opens and restores when it closes, marks the initial viewport-driven open as automatic, and tracks `_detailsAutoHidden` / `_detailsUserOverride` so an explicit re-open while docked is remembered for the session and never fought. The explicit-close path clears the preference. Commit `96778057` with the spec in `9a045c1b`; PR #227.

### Product value and UI visibility

Opening Settings or any docked tool window collapses Details so the chat gains the space, and closing the panel restores the previous state. If the user re-opens Details while a side panel is open, it stays open. The change is presentation only and uses the existing dock state layer.

### Verification

Source guards in `tests/test_details_autohide_wiring.py` report 4 passed; the browser spec `tests/browser/mad-932-details-autohide.spec.js` reports 6 passed covering Settings hide/restore, override persistence, the Compare overlay as a second dock, and wallboard/laptop/mobile widths without horizontal overflow; adjacent modal/UI batches pass and the full Python suite is reported green at the lane head.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No dependency, API, or data change. The "keep Details open while docked" preference lives in module state for the session (no localStorage), matching the panel's existing viewport-derived state model — a page reload returns to the default. Rollback is reverting the commit.
